speaker: Doctor
text: Let me start by asking: how many days postpartum are you, and what is the highest temperature you have recorded? Do you have any other symptoms like chills, nausea, or foul-smelling vaginal discharge?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Since you mentioned uterine tenderness and decreased bowel sounds, I need to clarify if you are experiencing any pain with urination or if your urine appears cloudy. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Urine Culture.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Pending; Urine Culture: Pending

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum Endometritis (likely with a co-existing urinary tract infection or pelvic abscess given the decreased bowel sounds and mass effect).

I am aware of the previous suggestion of anemia, but your primary presentation of high fever, uterine tenderness, and foul-smelling discharge is classic for infection. Given the "decreased bowel sounds" and significant uterine pain, I need to rule out a pelvic abscess or severe distension.

REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic Ultrasound.
REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential.
